title: Citizen manual: what a citizen can do on vote.ke

body:
# Citizen Manual

Living document: updated every time we ship. Covers everyone with a regular account (no campaign, no admin duties). Checked = live on vote.ke today.

## Getting started

As a visitor, I can create an account with my email and password, or with Google.
Click "Sign up", fill in your name and email (or pick "Continue with Google"), then confirm the code we email you.
As a visitor, I can sign up or log in without leaving the page I'm on.
Wherever an action needs an account (follow a leader, pledge a vote, save a ballot), a popup opens with the same login/signup forms; after the email code, you land right back where you were and the action completes itself.
As a citizen, I can log in and out.
"Log in" from the top of any page; "Log out" from the account menu.
As a citizen who forgot their password, I can reset it.
On the login page click "Forgot password", enter your email, and follow the link we send.
As a citizen, I must verify my email before using the dashboard.
Right after signup, enter the code from your inbox (in the popup, or on the "Verify email" page) or click the link in the email.
As a citizen who signed up with Google, I can set a password later.
The Account page shows "Set password" instead of "Change password" until you have one.

## My account

As a citizen, I can manage my personal details.
Visit Dashboard, then Account: edit your name, bio, and address.
As a citizen, I can set my county, constituency, and ward once on my account.
Account page dropdowns; optional, and used to prefill things like the ballot.
As a citizen, I can add and verify my phone (SMS), WhatsApp, and email without leaving the page.
On the Account page, type the number or address and click "Verify" next to it; a popup takes the code right there. A contact you have already verified (on any channel, or on a profile you manage) shows "Verified" instantly wherever you type it again.
As a citizen, I can change my password or delete my account.
Both from the Account page; deleting asks for confirmation first.

## Finding and comparing leaders

As a citizen, I can search for any leader by name.
Use the search page or the search box in the top bar.
As a citizen, I can jump from any page to any other with the quick search.
Click the small search box in the header (or press "/") and it expands over the menu; suggestions are grouped into Platform pages, Regions (counties, constituencies, wards), Executive, Parliament, MCAs, and Parties. Arrow keys move the highlight, Enter opens the pick, and "Search everything" hands the words to the full search page.
As a citizen, I can browse all leaders, parties, and alliances.
Visit "Leaders", "Parties", or "Alliances" from the main menu; each leader's name links to their public profile.
As a citizen, I can view a leader's public profile.
Their photo, bio, seat, party, track record, manifesto, and contact links live at vote.ke/their-name.
As a citizen, I can browse leaders by era.
A subtle line of year ranges (2022-now back to 2003 and earlier) under the directory filters reslices the register to who served in that era; a leader who served across several eras appears in each one, shown with the seat they held then.
As a citizen, I can read what each role or study actually involved.
Education and professional entries on a profile carry a short description under the title, not just an institution and dates.
As a citizen, I see leaders' real photos across the site.
Leader cards, seat pages, search results, profiles, and the ballot all show the leader's photo, with initials only when no photo exists yet.
As a citizen, I can see every seat and who is contesting it.
Visit a seat page like /mp/westlands or /governor/nairobi to see the current holder and all candidates.
As a citizen, I can compare two leaders side by side.
On any leader card, click the small compare button (top right corner) to pick leader A, then click "B" on another card; you land on a side-by-side comparison.
As a citizen, I can see leaders ranked by engagement.
Visit "Ranks" for a transparent public ranking.

## My ballot

As a citizen, I can step into the voting booth from any page.
The Ballot page (linked from the top bar and the homepage) is the ballot simulator: pick your county, constituency, and ward, then tap one candidate per seat (or skip a seat). Each seat step names its region ("Nairobi County") under the heading.
As a citizen, I can write in anyone for any seat.
Every seat step has a "Suggest someone else" search: pick any profile on the platform, whether or not they're vying for that seat. Your write-in shows as a chip you can clear.
As a citizen, I can share my ballot with friends.
After casting, you land on a share link (vote.ke/ballot/...) anyone can open to view your picks; no name, contact, or location below ward is ever shown on it. A WhatsApp button shares it in one tap; the Share button uses your phone's share sheet or copies the link.
As a citizen, I can save my ballot to my account.
"Save My Vote" on the ballot page (signing up in the popup if needed, the save finishes itself after). A ballot cast as a guest links itself to your account when you later sign up on the same device. Opening a friend's shared ballot, "Save This Vote" adopts a copy as your own.
As a citizen, I can see all my simulations on the My Vote tab.
Dashboard, then My Vote: a table with one row per saved simulation and one column per seat, each cell the actual leader picked; view any ballot or delete it (with confirmation).
As a citizen, I can pledge my 2027 vote to a candidate.
"Pledge" sits next to each candidate on a ballot page, and a "Pledge Your Vote" card sits on every campaign page and leader profile with an active run. Pledging needs a logged-in account (the popup opens if you're signed out); your pledges appear on My Vote grouped by seat, as full leader cards.
As a citizen, I can follow a candidate right from a shared ballot or a news article.
A compact "Follow" button next to the candidate expands into a name + phone-or-email form; no account needed, and campaign updates arrive on the channel you gave.
As a citizen, I can follow a leader from their profile or campaign page with one click.
Signed in, "Follow {name}" is a single button (no forms); "Unfollow" sits next to the title once followed. Signed out, the button opens the login popup and finishes the follow after.

## News and notifications

As a citizen, I can read news and filter it to leaders I follow.
The homepage news feed has filter buttons for each leader you actually follow, plus topic, mention, and region filters.
As a citizen, I can see my invites and notifications in one place.
Dashboard, then Notifications: campaign invites and decision notifications together; the bell in the header counts unread ones and deep-links here.

## Learning and contact

As a visitor, I can learn how registration and the six ballots work.
"Learn" (in the top bar) groups short voter-education articles by topic, with "Why vote?" featured first.
As a visitor, I can track key 2027 election dates and find registration drives.
The "Key Dates" page lists IEBC milestones (expected dates flagged as such); "Registration Drives" lists where to register, and "Verify Registration" walks through checking your voter status.
As a visitor, I can read why voting matters, what the platform does, and what it costs.
See the "Why vote?", "Features", "Pricing", "FAQ", and "About" pages. Leaders start at "For Leaders".
As a visitor, I can contact the team.
Use the "Contact us" page.

## Doing more

As a citizen, I can accept an invitation to join a campaign team.
Open the invite link you were sent, log in (or sign up), and you land in that campaign's dashboard.
As a citizen, I can become an ambassador for a campaign, see the Ambassador manual.
As a citizen, I can create or claim a leader profile, see the Leaders manual.

body:
# Ambassador Manual

Living document: updated every time we ship. An ambassador is a citizen who recruits supporters for a campaign: no separate account needed. Checked = live on vote.ke today.

## Becoming an ambassador

As a citizen, I become an ambassador by accepting a campaign's invitation.
A campaign manager sends you an invite link by email. Open it, log in (or sign up), and the ambassador role is added to your account.

## My workspace

As an ambassador, I can open my workspace for each campaign I serve.
The mode switcher at the top of the dashboard lists every campaign you're an ambassador for; pick one to open its workspace.
As an ambassador, I can sign up new supporters for the campaign.
In the workspace, enter a supporter's details to add them as a follower of the campaign.
As an ambassador, I can see my own recruits.
Your workspace lists only the people you personally signed up. The campaign's full follower roster stays with the managers.

## Staying a citizen

As an ambassador, everything in the Citizen manual still applies to me.
Your ballot, follows, reviews, and account settings are unchanged; ambassador duties are an extra tab, not a different account.

title: Leaders and campaign managers manual: getting on vote.ke and running a campaign

body:
# Leaders & Campaign Managers Manual

Living document: updated every time we ship. Covers leaders themselves and the people who run their campaigns (managers). A campaign manager can run several applications, claims, and campaigns from one account. Checked = live on vote.ke today.

## Starting a new leader profile (application)

As a campaign manager, I can start a leader application.
Visit Dashboard and click "Launch application". You get your own application workspace with tabs; the web address stays the same for the whole application, so you can come back anytime.
As a campaign manager, I can fill in the leader's profile.
On the Profile tab: first name, other names, bio, and the elective position (seat). Upload the leader's photo and IEBC Certificate of Clearance here too. Images open a crop step first, and every upload saves automatically (no extra submit button).
As a campaign manager, I can add experience entries with a short description.
Each added education or professional entry takes a title, institution, years, and an optional description (up to 500 characters) explaining what the role or study involved; the description shows under the entry on the public profile.
As a campaign manager, I can add the campaign's contact details.
On the Contacts tab: office address, phone, WhatsApp, and email, plus website and social links. You can save partially filled forms; whatever is still missing keeps a red star.
As a campaign manager, I can verify the campaign's phone and email without leaving the form.
Click "Verify" next to a contact and enter the code in the popup that opens. A number or address you already verified on your own account counts here too: it shows "Verified" right away and saves as verified, no second code.
As a campaign manager, I can build the team.
On the Team tab, invite at least one more person by email; each invitee gets a link that adds them to the campaign.
As a campaign manager, I always know what's missing.
The header line lists everything still required (replacing the status word until complete), and each tab title carries a star until it's done.
As a campaign manager, I can submit the application for review.
Once every tab is complete, click "Submit Application" (top right). An admin reviews it; if rejected, you see the reason and can fix things and resubmit.
As a campaign manager, I can delete a draft application.
"Delete" sits next to Submit; it asks for confirmation and removes the whole draft.

## Claiming an existing leader profile

As a campaign manager, I can claim a leader profile that already exists on the platform.
On the leader's public page, click "Claim this profile". If you are not logged in, you are asked to log in first and brought right back.
As a claimant, I fill in the same kind of tabs, but nothing touches the real profile until approval.
Profile, Contacts, and Signoff tabs; everything you enter is held as evidence for the reviewer.
As a claimant, I can verify contacts to prove they are mine.
Verifying a phone or email during a claim records the proof with your claim; the leader's public details stay untouched.
As a claimant, I sign off with my identity.
On the Signoff tab: your role in the campaign (pick from a list), your national ID number, and photos of your ID (front and back, with the same crop step).
As a claimant, I can submit or delete my claim.
"Submit Claim" and "Delete" sit at the top right. After submitting, an admin reviews it; the admin may also email the leader an approve link (see below).
As a claimant, my claim survives navigation.
A pending claim appears in the mode switcher, so you can leave and come back to it.

## Paying for your package

As a campaign manager, I pay for the package at the end of the onboarding wizard.
After picking the profile (claim or create) and the plan, the Complete Payment step sends you to a secure Paystack page where you pay by M-Pesa, card, or bank. When the payment goes through you land straight in the leader's dashboard.
As a campaign manager, I don't lose my payment if my connection drops.
Payment confirmation also arrives server-to-server, so even if you never make it back from the payment page, the profile and subscription are set up automatically and appear on your dashboard.
As a campaign manager, I get a receipt notification.
A notification (and email) confirms the plan, amount, payment reference, and subscription end date; platform admins are notified of the new campaign at the same time.
As a campaign manager, I'm reminded before my subscription lapses.
An email arrives 7 days before the end date, and another when the subscription expires. An expired subscription keeps the profile public but limits package features until renewal.

## The leader's own approval

As the leader being claimed, I can approve or reject a claim myself from my inbox.
When an admin sends it, you receive an email with a private link. Open it, review who is claiming your profile, and click Approve or Reject. The link works once; if you don't recognize the person, reject. Admins review every claim as well.

## Running a verified campaign

Once the application is approved, the campaign gets its own dashboard (reachable from the mode switcher).

### Profile and reach

As a manager, I can keep the profile up to date. Profile and Contacts tabs work as in the application.
As a manager, I can publish posts. Posts tab: write updates that appear on the public profile.
As a manager, I can maintain the manifesto. Manifesto tab: the campaign's promises, shown publicly.
As a manager, I can log what was delivered. Delivery tab: list concrete things delivered under a term or a non-elective role; pin up to 5 to show on the public profile.
As a manager, citizens can pledge their 2027 vote to my campaign.
A "Pledge Your Vote" card sits on the campaign page and the leader profile; pledging requires the citizen to be logged in, so every pledge is a real account.
As a manager, I can see and grow the follower list. Followers tab lists everyone following the campaign, including who recruited them. Citizens follow with one click from the profile/campaign page (logged in), or via the name + contact form on shared ballots and news.
As a manager, I can read reviews left by citizens. Reviews tab.

### Team

As a manager, I can invite and manage team members.
Team tab: send invites by email, set each member's role, and deactivate members who leave.
As a manager, my package sets how big the team and audience can grow.
Active manager and ambassador seats are capped per package (upgrade to add more; deactivating someone frees a seat), and new followers stop arriving once the package's citizen-subscription limit is reached. AI chat is available on every package and runs on the profile's credit balance.

### Money

As a manager, I can set a fundraising goal and track donations.
Fundraising tab: donations from the public page arrive as "pending" (donors send via M-Pesa manually); confirm each one against your statement.

### Outreach and intelligence

As a manager, I can send a broadcast to supporters in a chosen area.
Broadcasts tab: compose once, pick the geographic segment, send by email.
As a manager, I can watch press mentions.
PR desk tab: every news item that mentions the leader (pulled daily from news feeds), with sentiment chips and alerts on volume spikes or negative runs.
As a manager, I can cross-post to X and Facebook in one click.
"Post" / "Share" buttons on any public post (and on press mentions) open the network's composer prefilled with the headline and link. Post from whichever account is signed in.
As a manager, I can watch the competition.
Competitors tab: everyone else vying for the same seat, with their public numbers (followers, activity, coverage).

### AI Chat (verified campaigns only)

As a manager, I can control what the AI tells citizens.
Knowledge tab (unlocks once verified): write an FAQ and upload source documents (PDF, .txt, .md, with PDF text extracted automatically). The AI Chat feature on the public profile answers citizen questions ONLY from the FAQ, uploaded documents, and the Leader/Contacts/Delivery/Campaign/News/Broadcasts/Reviews/Competition tabs, never Team, Followers, or Fundraising, and never anything it wasn't given. The tab opens with a plain-language explainer of how this works, since it's the feature managers most often fear or misunderstand.

## Working across several campaigns

As a campaign manager, I can switch between everything I'm involved in.
The mode switcher (top of the dashboard) lists every campaign you manage ("Managing X"), every application in progress ("Applying X"), every pending claim ("Claiming X"), and any ambassador roles, plus your own citizen view and, for admins, the admin view.
